title: Write the approved copy, then the test that keeps it complete
outcome: A user who is stopped reads a zh-TW sentence naming what actually happened, and a reason added later without copy fails a test instead of degrading silently.
acceptanceCriteria: Every entry matches the copy inventory approved on the Design page. The inventory was settled before approval rather than during execution, so this slice writes agreed strings and does not decide wording.

The four reasons the inventory marks as gated by the UI still get copy. The gate is real — an owner never sees the leave control, and the transfer control renders only for the current owner — but SWR holds team membership for five minutes, so a client acting on stale data can still be refused by the server. Without an entry that refusal renders as the unknown-error message, which is the one case where we know exactly what happened and say we do not.

The exhaustiveness test derives its reason set from the exports of src/entities/errors/index.ts. A hand-written list is what dropped ProfileReason from the original scoping, and it would drop the next enum too.

The exhaustiveness test lands after the copy, not before. Landing it first makes placeholder strings the cheapest way to green, and a green test over placeholder copy reports a completeness that does not exist.
INVALID_EMAIL and PROFILE_NOT_FOUND get copy even though nothing displays them today. Their only call sites swallow the error or write their own; both become reachable as those sites are fixed.
